Durchlauchtigster Fürst

Gnädigster Fürst und Herr!

So eben ſchickt mein Pächter aus Schwammen herein und bittet mich dringend daß ich auf einen Augenblick heraus komme, und die Bauern in Ordnung bringen mögte die ihm nicht Folge leisten, sondern die Dienste versagt Ich muß nun schon dahin eilen um Unfug zu verhüten wollen.

Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht verzeihen woll höchst gnädigst daß ich heute dieser Sache wegen nicht auf den Mittag erscheinen Mitt dH. Minister habe ich heute wegen Schlabrendorff gesprochen, Aufrichtig gesagt, so scheint er es etwas krum zu nehmen, daß Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht ihm nichts sagen wollen, den ich glaube er hatt daß gestern erwartet - rech aber finde ich es gut daß Höchstdieselben ihm nichts sagen, mann kan ja erst sehen was er thun wird.

Er hatt an Schlabrendorff geschrieben daß er den 15ten daß

Monats hier sein soll er habe mit ihm in der Quist. Angelegenheit zu sprechen - vorläufig lege er ihm aus Herz sogleich alle Klage zurück zu nehmen, denn man paße so sehr auf ihm, daß auch nicht das mindeste unentdeckt bleiben würde und wann man eines Groſchens werth Mackel in der Sache finden mögte könte er versichert sein, daß es ihm traurig gehen dürfte.

Er der Minister könne ihm den Sch: auch hernach bey den besten Willen nicht retten ja, er müße es alsdann gerade hin verläugnen, daß er ihm durch Bande des Blutes verwand ſey p.p.

Dem Arch hatt er heute bey sich gehabt und ihm alles dies mündlich gesagt um es den Grafe in Stolze, wohin Asch übermorgen geht noch weiter ans Herz zu legen; besonders soll er Schlabrendorffen ja dahin vermögen daß er den 15ten d. hier sein soll?

Ich gehn morgen nach Landen, bei aber ganz gewis den 15 auch hier und da werde ich Hirsch mit anspannen- zu Tiefster Submission ersterbe

Ewr Hochfürstliche Durchlaucht

Breslau den 3ten Aug

1802

treu unterthäniger Knecht

v Triebenfeld

translation.en: Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! Just this moment my tenant from Schwammen sends in and urgently begs me to come out for a moment and set the peasants in order, who will not obey him, but have refused the labour services. I must now hasten thither in order to prevent mischief. Your Most Serene Highness will most graciously forgive that today, on account of this matter, I cannot appear at midday. With the Herr Minister I have spoken today concerning Schlabrendorff. Frankly said, he seems to take it somewhat amiss that Your Most Serene Highness will say nothing to him, for I believe he expected that yesterday - but I find it right and good that Your Highness says nothing to him; one may first see what he will do. He has written to Schlabrendorff that on the 15th of this

month he is to be here, that he has to speak with him in the Quist affair - for the present he lays it upon his heart to withdraw all complaint at once, for they are watching him so closely that not the least thing would remain undiscovered, and should anyone find so much as a Groschen's worth of blemish in the matter, he might be assured that it would go sadly with him. He, the Minister, could not thereafter save him, the said Sch:, even with the best will; indeed, he would then have to deny outright that he was related to him by ties of blood, etc. etc. Asch he had with him today and told him all this by word of mouth, so that it might be pressed further upon the heart of the Count at Stolze, whither Asch goes the day after tomorrow; in particular he is by all means to prevail upon Schlabrendorff that he be here on the 15th of this month? I go tomorrow to Landen, but shall quite certainly be here again on the 15th, and then I shall put Hirsch into harness as well. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Most Serene Highness's Breslau, the 3rd of August 1802 faithful humble and obedient servant [most faithful servant] v Triebenfeld

text_english:
Most Serene Prince, Most gracious Prince and Lord! Just this moment my tenant from Schwammen sends in and urgently begs me to come out for a moment and set the peasants in order, who will not obey him, but have refused the labour services. I must now hasten thither in order to prevent mischief. Your Most Serene Highness will most graciously forgive that today, on account of this matter, I cannot appear at midday. With the Herr Minister I have spoken today concerning Schlabrendorff. Frankly said, he seems to take it somewhat amiss that Your Most Serene Highness will say nothing to him, for I believe he expected that yesterday - but I find it right and good that Your Highness says nothing to him; one may first see what he will do. He has written to Schlabrendorff that on the 15th of this

month he is to be here, that he has to speak with him in the Quist affair - for the present he lays it upon his heart to withdraw all complaint at once, for they are watching him so closely that not the least thing would remain undiscovered, and should anyone find so much as a Groschen's worth of blemish in the matter, he might be assured that it would go sadly with him. He, the Minister, could not thereafter save him, the said Sch:, even with the best will; indeed, he would then have to deny outright that he was related to him by ties of blood, etc. etc. Asch he had with him today and told him all this by word of mouth, so that it might be pressed further upon the heart of the Count at Stolze, whither Asch goes the day after tomorrow; in particular he is by all means to prevail upon Schlabrendorff that he be here on the 15th of this month? I go tomorrow to Landen, but shall quite certainly be here again on the 15th, and then I shall put Hirsch into harness as well. In deepest reverence I remain, until death, Your Most Serene Highness's Breslau, the 3rd of August 1802 faithful humble and obedient servant [most faithful servant] v Triebenfeld
summary_en: Excuses himself from attending at midday because his tenant at Schwammen has called him out to deal with peasants refusing their labour services. Reports a conversation with the Herr Minister about Schlabrendorff: the Minister resents the Prince's silence, has summoned Schlabrendorff for the 15th over the Quist affair, and urges him to withdraw his complaint since he is closely watched and could not be protected. Asch carries this message to the Count at Stolze; Triebenfeld goes to Landen but will return by the 15th and also engage Hirsch.
summary_de: Entschuldigt sein Ausbleiben zur Mittagstafel: der Pächter aus Schwammen habe um sofortiges Erscheinen gebeten, da die Bauern ihm den Gehorsam und die Dienste verweigerten. Berichtet vom Gespräch mit dem Herrn Minister über Schlabrendorff, der dem Fürsten dessen Schweigen verüble; Schlabrendorff sei zum 15. d. M. hierher beschieden, um in der Quist'schen Sache zu sprechen, und solle alle Klage zurückziehen, da man ihn scharf beobachte und der Minister ihn dann nicht schützen könne. Asch reise übermorgen nach Stolze zum Grafen; Triebenfeld gehe morgen nach Landen, sei am 15. zurück und wolle dann auch Hirsch einspannen.
